fine_lines.title: had better vs should
fine_lines.explanation_ar: الاثنان لإعطاء النصيحة. had better أقوى من should وغير رسمية، وفيها معنى أن شيئًا سيئًا قد يحدث إن لم تفعل. بعدها فعل بدون to: You'd better go (وليس to go).
fine_lines.explanation_en: Both give advice. Had better is stronger and informal; it suggests something bad may happen if you don't. Use the base verb with no to: You'd better go.

examples.sentence: You'd better decide soon. It might sell out.

fine_lines.title: 'd better vs 'd rather
fine_lines.explanation_ar: الاختصار 'd في you'd better = you had better (نصيحة). أما في I'd rather = I would rather (تفضيل). بعد الاثنين فعل بدون to.
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'd in you'd better = had (advice). 'd in I'd rather = would (preference). Both take the base verb with no to.

fine_lines.title: lightning vs lighting
fine_lines.explanation_ar: lightning (بحرف n) = البرق في العاصفة. lighting = الإضاءة في مكان.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Lightning (with n) is the flash in a storm. Lighting is the lights in a room.

examples.sentence: The lighting in this room is too dark.

grammar.title: Had better and would rather
grammar.explanation_ar: 1) had better + فعل (بدون to): لإعطاء نصيحة قوية وغير رسمية، أقوى من should و ought to، وغالبًا تعني أن نتيجة سيئة قد تحدث: You'd better decide soon. نختصر had مع الضمائر: you'd better, I'd better. النفي: had better not: You'd better not be late. 2) would rather + فعل (بدون to): للتعبير عن التفضيل: I'd rather walk. ونختصر would مع الضمائر: I'd rather. وللمقارنة نستخدم than: I'd rather walk than take a taxi. انتبه: 'd قد تعني had أو would، والكلمة التي بعدها (better أو rather) تخبرك بالمعنى.
grammar.explanation_en: 1) Had better + base verb (no to): strong, informal advice, stronger than should and ought to; it often means something bad could happen: You'd better decide soon. Shorten had with pronouns: you'd better. Negative: You'd better not be late. 2) Would rather + base verb: to say what you prefer: I'd rather walk. Shorten would: I'd rather. Compare with than: I'd rather walk than take a taxi. Note: 'd can mean had or would; the next word (better or rather) tells you which.
examples: You'd better decide soon. Last year, it sold out.
If I had to choose, I'd rather be born a superhero.

questions.question: It's raining hard. You'd better ____ an umbrella.
questions.explanation_ar: بعد had better فعل بدون to.
questions.explanation_en: After had better, use the base verb.

questions.question: I'd rather ____ tea than coffee.
questions.explanation_ar: بعد would rather فعل بدون to.
questions.explanation_en: After would rather, use the base verb.

questions.question: In 'You'd better go,' 'd means:
questions.explanation_ar: الاختصار هنا يعني had: you had better.

questions.question: In 'I'd rather stay home,' 'd means:
questions.explanation_ar: الاختصار هنا يعني would: I would rather.

questions.question: Which is the strongest advice?
questions.explanation_ar: had better أقوى نصيحة بين هذه الخيارات.
questions.explanation_en: Had better is the strongest advice here.

questions.question: You'd better ____ late for the test.
'Sold out' means:
questions.explanation_en: Sold out means nothing is left.

questions.question: Impossible to see means ____.
questions.explanation_en: Invisible means you can't see it.

questions.question: A person you don't know is a ____.
questions.explanation_en: A stranger is someone you don't know.

questions.question: 'Take your time' means:
questions.explanation_en: It means there is no hurry.
